overview: This Senate resolution names the week beginning October 18, 2026, as "National Character Counts Week." It says good character is not automatic and that families, schools, faith communities, youth groups and civic organizations all help young people develop it. The resolution calls on Americans to embrace traits such as trustworthiness, respect, responsibility, fairness, caring and citizenship, as defined by local schools and communities, and to mark the week with ceremonies and activities. It does not create any program or spend any money. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on September 29, 2026.
for: Supporters say setting aside a week encourages schools and community groups to focus on teaching young people values like honesty, respect and responsibility.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or provide resources for character education programs.
